one_liner: Four hand-written SSE/AVX2 kernels that fuse colour conversion and threshold masking; first-party 3.4-7.6x over OpenCV call chains.
what_it_does: DeltaCV's CPU part is five free functions in namespace deltaCV (inRange, ycrcbWithSeg, weightedGrayWithSeg, grayBRWithSeg, grayBRWithSegStandard). Each takes a raw interleaved BGR (or one-channel) byte pointer plus width and height and writes an 8-bit 0/255 mask in one pass. They replace chains such as cv::cvtColor followed by cv::inRange, or cv::split plus Mat arithmetic plus cv::threshold. They are not drop-ins for single OpenCV calls. The repo also holds a few CUDA kernels (grey, an HSV-range mask, threshold, Otsu, Sobel, erode, histogram) and a Boost.Interprocess shared-memory publisher, none of which is packaged as a library.
how_it_is_fast: Kernel fusion: the colour transform and the range test run in registers on the same 16 or 32 pixels, so no intermediate YCrCb, grey or split-plane image is written to memory. BGR de-interleaving uses pshufb (_mm_shuffle_epi8) byte shuffles. The weighted sums are Q15 fixed-point dot products via pmaddwd (_mm_madd_epi16), packed back with saturation, and compared with unsigned max/min-plus-cmpeq tricks. ycrcbWithSeg and 3-channel inRange are 128-bit SSSE3/SSE4.1. weightedGrayWithSeg, both grayBR functions and 1-channel inRange use 256-bit AVX2, with the two 128-bit lanes split so the in-lane packus keeps pixel order.
when_to_use: Per-frame colour segmentation (robot vision, coloured-marker or light-bar detection) on x86 CPUs with AVX2, where the only output you need is a binary mask from a fixed BGR, grey-weight or channel-difference threshold.

Hot loops that today run cv::split plus scaled Mat adds plus cv::threshold (weightedGrayWithSeg) or a channel difference plus threshold (grayBRWithSegStandard). The fused pass avoids several full-image temporaries.
Plain 3-channel cv::inRange on contiguous 8-bit BGR images whose pixel count is a multiple of 16 (README: 0.29-0.30 ms vs 1.06-1.18 ms on 1024x1280).
As a reference or starting point for writing your own pshufb + pmaddwd fused kernels; each function is about 150 lines of intrinsics.
when_not_to_use: When the mask must match OpenCV's YCrCb: ycrcbWithSeg's colour math is wrong (see gotchas). Its Cr and Cb channels match neither BGR2YCrCb nor RGB2YCrCb, so thresholds tuned on cv::cvtColor output select different pixels.

Images whose pixel count is not a multiple of 16 (3-channel inRange, ycrcbWithSeg) or 32 (AVX2 functions): the scalar tail loop starts at a byte offset instead of a pixel index, so the trailing pixels are never written. For 1-channel inRange the tail reads two bytes past the buffer and trips an assert in debug builds.
Strided or ROI images (cv::Mat with padding or submatrices): there is no row-stride parameter, and every function assumes width*height*3 contiguous bytes.
Non-x86 targets or CPUs without AVX2: there is no scalar fallback, NEON path or runtime dispatch, and the build hard-codes -mavx2 -march=haswell.

The GPU part: the README's RGB2HSV speed-up compares an RGB mask kernel (it zeroes every non-negative hue) with a real OpenCV HSV conversion. GPU times exclude transfers and are set against a CPU, not OpenCV CUDA or NPP.

integration.dependencies: none for the SIMD kernels (raw pointers; core.hpp and DataTypes.hpp only include the intrinsics headers). OpenCV for the examples; Boost (system, atomic, interprocess) for shm.hpp and the CMake targets; CUDA plus OpenCV for the GPU part.
integration.min_toolchain: C++11 (CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 11); compiler not stated; built with -O3 -msse4.1 -mavx2 -march=haswell
integration.platforms: x86-64 with SSSE3/SSE4.1 for ycrcbWithSeg and 3-channel inRange and AVX2 for the rest (effectively Haswell or newer); GPU kernels need CUDA (tested on a GTX 1070)
integration.thread_safety: not documented; the CPU functions keep no global state and only touch caller buffers, so separate calls on separate buffers are independent
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — inRange mirrors cv::inRange for contiguous 8-bit images (pixel count a multiple of 16 or 32). The other functions fuse several OpenCV calls behind a new pointer-based signature, and ycrcbWithSeg does not reproduce OpenCV's YCrCb.

gotchas: Correctness bug behind the headline 7.4-7.6x row: ycrcbWithSeg mixes channel orders. The Y row treats channel 0 as blue (0.114, 0.587, 0.299). The Cr row (0.499, -0.419, -0.081) is RGB-order Cr, so channel 0 is treated as red. The Cb row (0.395, -0.331, -0.064) equals 0.564*(ch0 - Y_rgb), which is not Cb in either order. For a skin-tone BGR pixel (120,150,220) it yields (Y,Cr,Cb) = (168,107,112), where cv::cvtColor BGR2YCrCb gives (168,165,101) (derived by evaluating both formulas). The timed example also runs cv::COLOR_RGB2YCrCb on an imread (BGR) image, so neither side is the conversion the header documents.

grayBRWithSeg's color_mode is swapped against its header comment ('0 -> red, 1 -> blue'): mode 0 computes B-G and mode 1 computes R-G. The header and example suggest gray weights scalar_d(0.144,0.587,0.299), a typo for 0.114 that brightens grey by 3% and no longer matches the cv::COLOR_BGR2GRAY output it is compared with.

The SIMD and scalar-tail paths disagree. The SIMD path uses saturating unsigned subtraction and truncating Q15 shifts; the tail uses signed differences. Grey and weighted-grey values are truncated, not rounded, so they can be 1 below OpenCV's. ycrcbWithSeg is declared bool but returns nothing, which is undefined behaviour if the result is used.

There are no tests and no timing harness. Every example compares outputs by imshow; ycrcbWithSeg.cpp and grayBRWithSegStandard.cpp declare timers that are never used, and the former references an undeclared loop variable i, so it does not compile.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick DeltaCV only when you want a fused threshold mask in one pass and will fix and test the kernels yourself. For colour conversion that matches OpenCV, CompV (RGB to grey, YUV and HSV, 6-7x OpenCV in its own result file) or FlyCV are maintained libraries, and RGB2Y covers plain BGR-to-grey at 2-3x OpenCV.
verified_claims_summary: The README's same-machine CPU table (1024x1280 BGR, unnamed CPU and compiler, OpenCV version not stated, -O3 -mavx2 -march=haswell) reports the fused kernels at 3.4-7.6x OpenCV call chains, e.g. ycrcbWithSeg 0.88-0.90 ms vs cvtColor plus inRange 6.68-6.75 ms. The repo has no timing code to reproduce this, and the ycrcbWithSeg output does not match the OpenCV chain it was timed against. The GPU table (GTX 1070 kernel-only vs OpenCV on an i5-7500 CPU) is not a like-for-like comparison.
status_note: Abandoned since 2019-04-27 (58 commits, one open issue from 2018 that says the interface is awkward to use). MIT-licensed and small enough to vendor, but treat it as unreviewed sample code: fix the YCrCb coefficients and the tail loops before shipping it.
